name: Concourse
tagline: Self-tuning document-graph database with automatic indexing, full version history and time-travel reads.
description: Concourse, from Cinchapi, is an open-source Java database whose records are schemaless documents made of keys that can each hold several values, with links between records forming a graph. Every write is versioned, so you can read a value as it was at any earlier moment or audit how it changed, and every value is indexed automatically, including substring indexing of strings for search, so ad-hoc range, predicate and text queries work without planning indexes. It provides serializable ACID transactions, the CCL criteria language and an interactive shell (CaSH). Development continues: 1.0.x images are published on Docker Hub, a 1.1 line is in progress, and a peer-to-peer distributed mode is documented but still alpha. The public GitHub repository returned 404 when checked in October 2026.

scale.notes: Single-node in production; the distributed CP mode with replication is documented as alpha.

strengths: Every value indexed automatically, so ad-hoc predicates and substring search need no index planning
Full version history with time-travel reads and change audits
Serializable ACID transactions over schemaless records
Links between records model graphs without join tables
weaknesses: Small community and few third-party integrations
Indexing every value costs extra storage and background work
Public source repository was unavailable when last checked
useCases: Applications that need audit trails and point-in-time reads
Exploratory data where queries are not known in advance
Integrating heterogeneous records with search across them
